title: What is OTC Crypto Trading and How Does it Work?
summary: Crypto OTC trading refers to large digital asset transactions executed outside of public exchanges.
body_markdown:
Crypto OTC trading refers to large digital asset transactions executed outside of public exchanges.


Institutional investors, hedge funds, and high-net-worth individuals trade over the counter through a crypto OTC trading platform, commonly known as an OTC desk. Unlike an order placed on Coinbase or Binance, these trades are arranged through dealer networks rather than a centralized public exchange. The process takes longer at times, but it carries several benefits: greater privacy,[deeper liquidity](https://www.bitgo.com/resources/blog/crypto-liquidity/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=prime&utm_campaign=what_is_otc) , minimal market disruption, and often better pricing.


OTC trading isn’t only about size. It comes with its own mechanics, costs, and risks. Here’s what to know before placing a trade.


## Key Takeaways


-


OTC means “over the counter.” The meaning of OTC in crypto is a trade negotiated privately between two counterparties and settled off exchange, rather than matched on a public order book.


-


It exists to solve market impact. A large exchange order walks the book and moves the price against the trader. This is called slippage. An OTC quote is one firm price for the entire buy.


-


Desks are either agency or principal. Agency desks broker the trade for a commission; principal desks quote from their own balance sheet and absorb the market risk.


-


Minimums can be high. Most desks start in the six-figure range, which puts crypto OTC trading out of reach for retail-sized orders.


-


There’s no clearinghouse. If the other side of an OTC trade fails to deliver, nothing backs it up. Pick the desk carefully.


## How Crypto OTC Trading Works


Crypto OTC trading platforms facilitate large-scale transactions between buyers and sellers. There are two primary types:


-


Agency desks charge a brokerage fee in exchange for connecting parties that trade directly.


-


[Principal desks](https://bitgo.com/resources/blog/regulated-otc-institutional-otc-desks-and-crypto-block-trades/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=prime&utm_campaign=what_is_otc_crypto_trading) assume market risk by using their own funds to purchase assets before reselling to interested buyers.


A typical trade moves through four stages:


-


Initiation. A trader contacts an OTC desk expressing interest in buying or selling, outlining asset type, volume, preferred pricing, and any other requirements. Onboarding and KYC checks are completed before a quote is issued.


-


Quotation. Agency desks connect interested parties, while principal desks provide price quotes based on market conditions.


-


Negotiation. Parties discuss and agree on terms.


-


Execution. Desks facilitate the trade, safeguarding it with secure payment channels, escrow, and/or custody services.


Settlement is where OTC structurally diverges from exchange trading. On an exchange, you prefund: assets must sit on the venue before you can trade, exposed to that venue’s balance sheet for as long as they remain there. A desk connected to qualified custody lets you trade directly from custody instead. Assets never leave the custodial environment, and settlement can occur in crypto, fiat, or stablecoin, on a timeline both sides agree to.


This is a structural difference between the two models. Prefunding determines how much capital sits idle across venues and how much exposure a firm carries to any single counterparty.


## Finding an OTC Desk


With large transactions at stake, desk selection should be carefully evaluated. Here are six things worth working through:


-


Regulatory status and licensing. Which legal entity faces you, and under which regulator?


-


Custody model. Must assets leave custody in order to trade, or can the desk execute against custodied balances?


-


Insurance coverage. What is insured, for how much, and by whom?


-


Settlement flexibility. Crypto, fiat, and stablecoin options, plus off-exchange settlement.


-


Breadth of supported assets. OTC desk crypto coverage varies widely, confirm support beyond BTC and ETH, including less liquid tokens.


-


Product coverage. Does the desk quote spot only, or spot alongside derivatives? Consolidating both with one counterparty means a single onboarding, one credit relationship, and one settlement workflow.


## OTC Crypto Trading vs. Exchange Trading


Both routes end with the same asset in the same wallet. What differs is how the price is formed and who sees the order. Exchanges are order-book venues: price is discovered publicly, and every resting bid and ask is visible. An OTC desk negotiates one price bilaterally, and the trade becomes visible only afterward, if at all. Some venues blur the line, an OTC crypto exchange may run both a public book and a block desk under one roof. What matters is which mechanism your order actually touches.

## OTC Crypto Derivatives


Spot isn’t the only thing that trades over the counter. Some desks also facilitate OTC crypto derivatives: options, forwards, swaps, and structured products negotiated bilaterally rather than listed on an exchange.


Institutions use these for two purposes. The first is hedging, a miner locking in a forward price on future production, or a treasury buying downside protection on a large BTC position without selling it. The second is customized exposure: a payoff profile, tenor, or strike no listed contract matches.


Because the terms are negotiated, OTC derivatives can be tailored in ways listed products cannot. That flexibility carries more counterparty risk than a cleared, exchange-traded contract, since performance depends on the other side rather than on a clearinghouse.


Derivatives are a more selective offering than spot OTC. Facilitating them requires the right licensing, collateral and margin infrastructure, plus risk systems built for non-linear exposure. Not every desk that quotes spot also quotes structures, availability varies by jurisdiction and client type.


## Benefits of Crypto OTC Trading


For institutional investors, hedge funds, or high-net-worth individuals, OTC trading offers distinct advantages over traditional exchanges. Instead of posting an order to a public book, the trade happens directly between two parties or through an intermediary, with terms and prices negotiated privately. That produces several benefits:


-


**Market stability:** Large trades on public exchanges can trigger volatility and flash crashes. Because OTC desks work with multiple liquidity providers, they reduce the risk of one large transaction moving market prices.


-


**Privacy:** Confidentiality is a major benefit of OTC trading. Unlike exchange transactions, these trades stay off-book, protecting traders from market speculation, front-running, and unwanted attention.


-


**Competitive prices:** OTC trading can offer better pricing and lower transaction costs than exchanges, through direct negotiation and reduced fees.


-


**Customized solutions:** Crypto OTC trading often features personalized service, including tailored pricing,[flexible settlement options](https://www.bitgo.com/products/settlement/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=prime&utm_campaign=what_is_otc_crypto_trading) , and high-touch customer service.


## Risks and Challenges of Crypto OTC Trading


Crypto OTC trading presents numerous benefits, but it’s worth being aware of the risks and challenges.


Take a scenario where a prominent crypto holder plans to sell 5% of their bitcoin (BTC). If that information leaked, other players could take advantage by front-running the trade. That’s why it’s important to work with trading desks that are both reputable and discreet.


Even if you work with a discreet broker, moves large enough to shift the market are bound to attract attention. Desks use various strategies to mitigate this risk, such as breaking trades into smaller chunks, spreading transactions across multiple liquidity providers, or leveraging private liquidity pools.


However, no system is entirely foolproof. The interconnected nature of crypto markets means small signals could tip off sophisticated traders. That’s why it’s essential to work with an established OTC desk that understands market dynamics.


Other challenges include:


-


**Counterparty risk:** One party defaults or fails to fulfill their obligations.


-


**Market manipulation:** Thin order books, wash trading, and spoofing on reference venues can distort the prices an OTC quote is benchmarked against.


-


**Regulatory uncertainty:** The laws surrounding crypto vary by jurisdiction and are continually shifting. Participants must ensure compliance with local laws to avoid legal complications.


-


**Limited accessibility:** Due to high minimum transactions, crypto OTC desks may not be suitable for retail investors.


-


[Prefunding requirements:](https://www.bitgo.com/products/go-network-oes/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=prime&utm_campaign=what_is_otc_crypto_trading) Some OTC desks require trades to be prefunded. Investors wanting to be more capital-efficient should choose a desk without these requirements.


-


**Operational risks:** The private nature of OTC trades can make them susceptible to fraud or misrepresentation. This is especially problematic for initial coin offerings (ICOs), where inexperienced traders can be taken advantage of.


To help mitigate these risks, it's crucial to work with established brokers with strong track records of successful transactions. ## FAQs


### How does crypto OTC trading differ from traditional exchanges?


Unlike exchange-based trading, where buy and sell orders are publicly listed on an order book, OTC trades are conducted privately between two parties or an intermediary. This allows large transactions to be executed without alerting the market and triggering price slippage.


OTC desks also offer high-touch customer service and personalized services such as flexible settlement options, negotiation, and lower fees than charged by public exchanges.


### When does an OTC trade make more sense than using an exchange or algorithmic execution?


When the order is large relative to the book depth, when certainty of completion outweighs working an order over hours, or when the position is sensitive.


### What types of transactions can be conducted through OTC trading?


Not all crypto OTC trading platforms support the same transactions, but in general, most desks support crypto-to-crypto, crypto-to-fiat, and multi-asset swaps. Additionally, OTC desks support phased execution, block trades, and other structured transactions tailored for institutional clients.


### What is the difference between an agency OTC desk and a principal OTC desk?


An agency desk brokers between two counterparties for a commission. A principal desk trades against you from its own book, taking the market risk and earning the spread.


### How are OTC quotes, spreads, and fees determined?


Quotes reference prevailing market prices, then adjust for size, liquidity, and settlement terms. Principal desks earn the spread; agency desks charge a commission.


### What minimum trade sizes do crypto OTC desks typically require?


Minimums commonly start around $100,000, though thresholds vary by desk and asset. Less liquid tokens carry higher minimums.


### Does an OTC trade need to be prefunded, and can assets remain in qualified custody?


It depends on the desk. Some require prefunding; others execute against assets in qualified custody, so the position never leaves custody.


### How can institutions reduce counterparty and settlement risk in an OTC trade?


Confirm the desk's regulatory status and licensing, keep assets in qualified custody until settlement, settle off exchange rather than prefunding a venue, and confirm insurance coverage.


### What should institutions evaluate when selecting a crypto OTC desk?


Regulatory status, custody model, insurance coverage, settlement flexibility, breadth of supported assets, and product coverage.
